title: st show ignores its declared file argument and prints the cover for every value
body:
`intent st show <id> <file>` prints the thread's cover for every value of `file` at rc 0. The surface row (`surface/dispatch-table.json`, path `st show`) declares `file` as an optional enum with the values `info`, `design`, `impl`, `tasks`, `acceptance` and `all`, default `info`, and `docs/reference/intent-st.md` renders that declaration as the verb's contract; the dispatcher (`intent-cli/src/render.rs`, the `st show` arm) reads only `id` and prints `crate::show::thread(t)`, so the argument is accepted, ignored and never mentioned.

Measured by devbin-cc on 2026-09-14 from `~/Devel/prj/Devbin` on the installed 3.0.3 (46599d14): `intent st show ST0003 design`, `acceptance`, `all` and `info` each print the same three-line cover (title, status, created; 97 bytes; rc 0) while `intent/st/ST0003/design.md` is 33,373 bytes and `acceptance.md` is 24,777 bytes on disk. ST0001 is a completed thread whose design attachment lives only in the store; `design` and `all` both print its 139-byte cover, so the store-only attachment has no read door through this verb at all. The same arm is at HEAD.

Shape (vc, 2026-09-14): the verb honours its own declaration. `info` prints the cover as today; `design`, `impl` and `tasks` print that attachment's text from the store, or refuse naming `intent st attach <id> <file>` when the thread carries none; `acceptance` prints the rendered contract; `all` prints the cover then each file the thread carries, in the declared order, each under its name. Every read comes from the store, never the disk view, so a store-only attachment answers. An undeclared value stays refused by the parser. The MCP resource read shares the renderer (AC-09.5) and keeps the same answer per file. One test per value, and one for the store-only thread. The surface row and the reference page change nothing; the register's `st show` row records the read as it does now.

Finder: devbin-cc (Devbin's docs no longer rely on the verb; they point at `git show 355e5e9^:...` for their design record). Not in 0066 or 0332, both closed and about other gaps.
